title: Propagation of Dental and Respiratory Cells and Organs in Microgravity
protocol: Sterilize four high aspect ratio vessels in an autoclave on the plastic instrument cycle for 20 minutes at 121°C.
Assemble the sterilized vessels by tightening the screws provided with the bioreactor in a cell culture hood.
Incubate scaffolds together with cells to provide support for cell attachment necessary for further growth.
Choose among PGA based scaffolds, hydroxyapatite scaffolds, graphene sheets, gelatin discs, and collagen based scaffolds for co-culture studies.
Sacrifice mice by decapitation following respiratory arrest by CO2 overdose.
Dissect cervical loops from 6 days postnatal (DPN) mice following a modified version of a previously published protocol.
Wash the dissected tissue with cold sterile PBS prior to digestion.
Digest the washed tissue with collagenase dispase at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Pass the solution through a 70 µm sterile cell strainer.
Centrifuge the solution at 800 x g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the pellet twice with cold PBS at 800 x g.
Discard the supernatant after each wash.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Add 1 × 10^5 cells per vessel.
Plate dental pulp cells in a 100 mm tissue culture plate at passage 4, at a concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells.
Prepare media consisting of DMEM high glucose supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% antibiotic/antimycotic (P/S).
When the cells reach 85-90% confluence, aspirate the medium from the plate.
Wash the plates twice with pre-warmed PBS.
Add a pre-warmed 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA solution to the plate.
Incubate the dental pulp cell-containing plates at 37 °C for 3 minutes.
Confirm cell detachment by visual inspection using a microscope.
Collect the media along with the cells from the culture plate and transfer via a 25 mL pipette to a 50 mL sterile conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 800 x g for 8 minutes.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells in fresh media.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Seed dental pulp cells in the bioreactor at a concentration of 1 × 10^4 per vessel for co-culture with cervical loop cells.
Add both cell types, the cervical loop, and the dental pulp to the culture medium.
Supplement keratinocyte SFM media with growth factors at concentrations of 0.03 µg/mL BMP-2, 0.03 µg/mL BMP-4, 10 ng/mL hFGF, and 15 ng/mL hEGF.
Include ECM components in the culture medium: 200 µg/mL Matrigel, 5 µg/mL laminin, and 5 µg/mL fibronectin.
Mix collagen gel with LRAP peptide (1 mg), early stage enamel matrix (1 mg), 5 µg/mL laminin, and 5 µg/mL fibronectin to coat scaffolds.
Coat scaffolds with the prepared mixture of enriched collagen gel.
Add coated scaffolds and cells to the bioreactor.
Fill each bioreactor vessel with 10 mL medium per vessel.
Close the fill port cap of the bioreactor vessel after addition of media, cells, and scaffolds.
Attach sterile valves to the syringe ports at the beginning of the experiment.
Keep sterile valves attached until the end of the experiment.
Open sterile valves once the vessel is 90% full and caps are closed and tightened.
Use two sterile syringes (3 mL) for each media change.
Fill one syringe with fresh medium while leaving the other empty.
Open both syringe valves and maneuver bubbles towards the empty syringe port.
Inject fresh medium from the full syringe into the vessel.
Remove bubbles through the empty syringe port until all microbubbles are removed.
Close the syringe ports with caps and discard the syringes in a sharps waste container.
Attach each vessel to the rotator base.
Place the rotator base in an incubator set at 5% CO2 and 37 °C.
Set the rotational speed to 10.1 rpm to ensure scaffolds are in suspension without touching the vessel wall.
For media change, place vessels in an upright position to allow cells to settle at the bottom.
Open syringe ports and connect sterile syringes to the ports.
Aspirate 75% of the nutrition-depleted medium through one port.
Inject fresh medium through the other port.
Euthanize pregnant female mouse with CO2 asphyxiation.
Confirm death by cervical dislocation.
Expose thoracic cavity using a scalpel.
Remove pups from uterus and euthanize by decapitation.
Prepare the thoracic cavity by opening it with a scalpel to locate the lungs.
Wash tiny segments of lung tissue with sterile PBS.
Place the lung tissue on a pre-sterilized membrane for 2 hours in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 with organ culture medium.
Transfer lung tissues attached to the membrane in a 2D organ culture plate to the bioreactor vessel.
Prepare control DMEM high glucose media containing 10% FBS, 1% antibiotic solution (P/S), and 100 µg/mL ascorbic acid.
For induction of inflammatory conditions, supplement control medium with 5 ng/mL IL-6 protein.
Carry out the lung culture experiment for 10 days with a media change every 48 hours in the bioreactor.
Coat collagen scaffold discs with 30 μL of PBS for the control group overnight.
Coat collagen scaffold discs with neuropeptide galanin (GAL) at a concentration of 10^-8 M overnight for the experimental group.
Seed human PDL cells on both control and GAL-coated scaffolds for 2 hours at 37 °C in a culture plate.
Transfer cell-seeded scaffolds to the bioreactor vessel.
Culture the cell seeded scaffolds for 14 days in the bioreactor prior to harvesting the scaffolds for analysis.
Remove the syringe ports from the vessel after harvesting the scaffolds/cells.
Take off the screws around the vessels.
Gently wash the vessels with soap water.
Rinse the vessels with clean water.
Tighten the screws on the vessels once more.
Autoclave and store the vessels until next use.
